warning_texts: This profile is single-vendor: every context in this run, including this red team, is claude-opus-5. Isolated contexts are not independent reviewers, the chain of PASSes proves nothing on its own, and no GPT gate or other cross-vendor review exists anywhere in this system.

The only layer that really holds here is the deterministic one: the machine gates, the frozen check_plan, the control lock and the release surface gate. This red-team verdict does not replace any of them.

Writes to raw sources and frozen machinery were closed only by permissions.deny, which covers edit tools and not the shell. A modified raw file would be caught by the control lock after the fact, not prevented.

The evidence of all five LLM auditor steps is a placeholder note with no recalculation: gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor and gate_release_auditor. So their PASS verdicts carry no evidence anyone can verify.
gate0_semantic, gate_release_auditor and all four worker results each report one check whose expected and actual value is 0.473684. That value matches no figure in this dataset.

Every worker and auditor result has created_at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. That is earlier than the analysis plan's registered_at (2026-04-02), so the value cannot come from a clock and the run's timeline cannot be rebuilt from the results.
None of the worker results has a disclosures field, and all have empty warnings. No stage reported any deviation, and I cannot tell whether that means none happened or none was recorded.

No deterministic rule reads the text of analysis/answers, the population statements on the release surfaces, or card-level populations on the dashboard. On these points my judgment is the only check, and blockers 1 and 2 were found there.

The free_text_quarantined gate covers the register, the surfaces and stage results, but not analysis/answers. I could not tell whether the causal sentence in R04 came from the quarantined comment column. Its distinctive words are not among the manifest's top tokens. Someone with raw access should co

Assumption dedup_rule (latest_revision_wins) moves published numbers. In 126 of the 917 repeated orders the later revision turns pending or cancelled into delivered, so net revenue is 3,023,296.61 EUR here against 3,010,704.83 under first-revision-wins. The completion rates move by 0.22 points (dire

The dedup rule relies on file order more than updated_at can confirm. The last row in the file never has an earlier updated_at than the other revision, but in 549 of the 917 repeated orders both revisions share the same timestamp, so file order alone picks the current one.

Assumption shipping_locale looks wrong in scale. Read as declared, shipping is larger than the order's gross amount on 39,368 of 41,883 readable orders (median 901.14 against median gross 108.31), and shipping_total (37,792,722.50 EUR) is 12.5 times net revenue. That looks like a unit or scale error

Assumption date_input_formats (the slashed form is month-first) holds on the data. All 6,852 slashed dates agree with order_month when read month-first, and only 231 would agree if read day-first. It moves no published number, because the period is taken from order_month.

The report's channel caveats and the note under By channel say 'one quarter of orders'. That can read as 25% of orders rather than all orders of one calendar quarter; the figures cover every order in the quarter's population.

Both p values show as 0.0000 on the report and the dashboard, and on the dashboard the test cards give 0.0000 as their headline value under a bare label such as 'Test Channel Aov'. A reader can take that as p equal to zero or as no effect; 'p < 0.0001' would be accurate.

The AOV lines in the report and the AOV cards on the dashboard do not say 'delivered orders only' in their own caveats, although the population is delivered orders (n 17,818 and 12,055). The dashboard has no card-level population field at all.

The release contract declares no reconciliations and no card_caveat_requirements, so no gate checks headline against components. My own reconciliations hold (evidence/reconcile_output.json), but nothing will catch a future break.

The analysis plan does not say which Cohen's d formula to use. The published 0.4869 uses the pooled standard deviation; the average-variance form would give 0.4950. It does not change the conclusion, but the effect's definition was not registered.

H-CHANNEL-COMPLETION assumes neither channel changed how it books orders during the quarter. Monthly completion is stable (direct 0.719-0.732, partner 0.595-0.616), which is consistent with that but does not prove it.
The handoff has no drift_since_review field, which does not show that the stage code's assumptions hold on this export. Channel mix by country and by month is stable across the quarter.

The three renamed columns (customer_id, order_date, country) are covered by no values_preserved rule in the check plan. My row-by-row trace against the quarantine projection found 0 mismatches, but no gate will catch a future regression.

I could not verify the following, because they are outside my inputs: raw_data/questions.md (the exact wording of the question R04 answers), the src/ generator and analysis code (I relied on gate_release_machine and figures_not_hardcoded), whether audit/schemas/carry.schema.json accepts the carries,
Retry history and stale inputs are not visible to me. They are in 'audit_runner.py report', and I make no claim about them.
